yang: Heads up — eu1 warm pool had a sharp spike at 11:02 UTC, queue depth ~2200, p95 token latency jumped to 1.9s. Seen a bunch of spot preemptions in the last 10m. autoscaler-bot posted a snapshot below.
autoscaler-bot: ALERT eu1 autoscaler: queue=2200, running_gpus=420, pending_nodes=12, spot_terms=7 in 10m window. recent_scale_in=8 nodes/12m.
maria: Oof. Do we know if the scale-in aggressiveness is the main cause or are we losing capacity from spot churn + slow replacement?
kevin: I pulled the node events — multiple AZ terminations + kube-provisioner backoff. Our scale-in cooldown is 120s and replacement window for spot is ~180s, so we get hammered before preallocs kick in.
julia: Suggestion: try a short-term preheat (preallocated GPUs in warm pool) and increase scale_in_cooldown. Proposed config snippet: ```yaml
autoscaler:
  preheat_fraction: 0.20  # keep 20% spare during observed surge windows
  scale_in_cooldown: 300   # avoid oscillating scale-in during spot churn
  smoothing_window: 45s
```
yang: Also think we should gate admission with a soft-token-bucket per-region while preheat ramps. Something like `bucket_capacity=1000, rate=250/s, burst=500` so clients get soft-queued responses instead of blowing out the runtime. That reduces tail latency while preheat finishes.
kevin: Cost note — preheating GPUs will increase billed GPU-hours. We should limit to peak windows and have dynamic preheat tied to historical traffic and forecasts. Maybe enable preheat only for eu1 between 10:30-13:30 UTC for the canary.
maria: OK let's define the experiment: deploy preheat_fraction=0.20 + scale_in_cooldown=300 to eu1 as a 15% canary for 48h. Success criteria: reduce queue depth p95 by >=70% during spikes and keep extra GPU-hours <= 8% over baseline. Rollback if error rate or latencies get worse.
julia: I'll open the rollout and runbook. Canary command: `deploy canary autoscaler-config eu1 --pct 15 --duration 48h`. Runbook steps include rollback `deploy canary autoscaler-config eu1 --pct 0` and alerting thresholds.
sre-ops: Also add a watch on spot churn rate and kube-provisioner backoff logs; if spot_terms > 5 in 15m, abort canary and notify infra-oncall.
yang: Agree. After canary, if it looks good we can add a small dynamic preheat window with historical weekday profiles to avoid constant costs. I'll put a short write-up in the postmortems channel if we need deeper analysis. :thumbsup:
maria: Thanks — will sync after canary metrics land.
